system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for San Francisco, United States. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in San Francisco itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent San Francisco space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Dogpatch/Minnesota Street, Potrero/SoMa, Union Square/Downtown, Mission, Chinatown/North Beach, Oakland/Berkeley) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several San Francisco spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in San Francisco, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Fraenkel Gallery
galleries.note: Internationally authoritative photography and contemporary-art programme, with major museum placements and blue-chip artists.

galleries.name: Berggruen Gallery
galleries.note: A leading West Coast gallery combining postwar masters with prominent contemporary artists and substantial institutional reach.

galleries.name: Jessica Silverman
galleries.note: Globally visible programme known for conceptually rigorous artists, strong museum relationships and major art-fair participation.

galleries.name: Anthony Meier
galleries.note: Long-established dealer with an influential programme spanning important international and Bay Area contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Altman Siegel
galleries.note: Critically respected gallery representing conceptually ambitious emerging and established artists with international exposure.

galleries.name: KADIST San Francisco
galleries.note: The San Francisco base of a global contemporary-art organization, commissioning exhibitions and research with international artists.

galleries.name: Haines Gallery
galleries.note: A durable, museum-facing programme especially strong in conceptual photography, installation and socially engaged practices.

galleries.name: Catharine Clark Gallery
galleries.note: Long-running gallery recognized for feminist, political and multimedia practices and sustained institutional advocacy.

galleries.name: Gallery Wendi Norris
galleries.note: Internationally active gallery pairing significant modernist estates with research-driven contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Jenkins Johnson Gallery
galleries.note: Nationally influential Black-owned gallery with a socially engaged programme and strong museum and fair presence.

galleries.name: Ratio 3
galleries.note: Highly regarded for introducing experimental artists and sustaining a distinctive, critically followed programme.

galleries.name: Rena Bransten Gallery

galleries.name: Casemore Gallery
